stem: The President resigns, and the Vice-President becomes President to serve the unexpired term. She serves as President for five years. Under Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution, may she later be elected President?
choices: Yes, because she was never elected as President
Yes, but only after one full term has passed
No, because she served as President over four years
No, because no Vice-President may run for President
answer: No, because she served as President over four years
hints: She was not elected President; she succeeded to the office. Notice how long she served.
Article VII, Section 4 has a special rule for a person "who has succeeded as President". Find the number of years in that rule.

That rule bars a successor who served more than a certain number of years, and it ends with the words "at any time". Compare her five years with that number, then decide whether waiting a term would change anything.

solution.methodName: Match the situation to the provision

steps.action: Identify her situation: she became President by succession, not by election.
steps.why: Article VII, Section 8 says that if the President resigns, "the Vice-President shall become the President to serve the unexpired term."

steps.action: Read the rule in Article VII, Section 4: "No person who has succeeded as President and has served as such for more than four years shall be qualified for election to the same office at any time."
Compare: she served five years, which is more than four.
steps.why: So the rule applies to her even though she was never elected President.
The bar never ends, so waiting one term does not help.

steps.action: No, she may not be elected President, because she served as President for more than four years.

trapNotes.Yes, because she was never elected as Pr: Section 4 covers successors too. A person who "has succeeded as President" and served more than four years is barred, even if never elected.
trapNotes.Yes, but only after one full term has pa: The bar applies "at any time", so waiting a term does not remove it.
trapNotes.No, because no Vice-President may run fo: Section 4 does not bar every Vice-President. Only a person who succeeded as President and served more than four years is barred.
